o.text:
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *yuŋ.
Cognates
Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (yüŋ), Turkish yün, Turkmen ýüň, Tatar йон (yon), Kazakh жүн (jün), Kyrgyz жүн (jün), Uzbek jun, Bashkir йөн (yün), Tuvan чүң (çüñ) Nogai юн (yun), Crimean Tatar yün, Khakas нӱң (nüñ), Karachay-Balkar джюн (cün), Kumyk юн (yun), Chagatai [script needed] (yüŋ), Southern Altai јуҥ (ǰuŋ) / јум (ǰum), Uyghur يۇڭ (yung).
From Proto-Turkic *nē- (“what”). Compare Turkmen nǟme (“what”), Kazakh немене (nemene, “what”).

Morphologically çatmaq (“to reach”) + -dır. Cognate with Turkish çattırmak.
The sense 'drive, bring' is possibly a calque of Russian доводить (dovoditʹ).
From yapış + -qan. Cognate with Turkish yapışkan.

glosses: to ride a horse without bridle, by holding its mane

o.text: Izafet II compound of ana + xaqanlıq. Calque of English matriarchy.
